# What GitHub does with Mermaid (observed 2026-11-07)

Method: headless Chromium (Playwright's bundled build, dark colour scheme, not logged in) loaded existing public github.com pages and read the DOM of the page and of each `viewscreen.githubusercontent.com` iframe. The frame's own script (`/static/assets/mermaidMarkdown-5b99bd9a2037271fa4cf.js`, its stylesheet and the lazy chunks 697, 7150, 1620, 1873, 9822) was downloaded and read. No screenshots of github.com, nothing created on GitHub.

Pages used:
- https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/docs/syntax/mindmap.md
- https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/mermaid@11.16.1/docs/config/layouts.md
- https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/mermaid@11.16.1/docs/syntax/flowchart.md
- https://github.com/MarcoClementi/esercizio_info/blob/57b1fba0be0af45c9f084616c6322771b6e2db88/es7.md (fence is "```Mermaid")
- https://github.com/epabst/orchestrator-loop-for-ai/blob/main/README.md (a broken diagram)
- ELK front matter: https://github.com/knative/docs/blob/9b66fd97eea9a9251060102d05741d3b292dedfb/docs/versioned/serving/config-network-adapters.md, https://github.com/owid/owid-grapher/blob/1c67f2d3053555446f13215b596988089dd4cb4a/site/search/README.md, https://github.com/OpenDevicePartnership/patina/blob/39bfba7523a6930b1535d9a585fc2cf13634811b/docs/src/dxe_core/events.md, https://github.com/nvpro-samples/vk_minimal_latest/blob/14f31142bc2faf71e19a5bf00c59a3d0c3c60c26/README.md

## Version (changes the plan)
GitHub runs **Mermaid 12.2.0**, not 11.16.1: the bundle calls `renderer.draw(id, text, "12.2.0", diagram)`. The default look in 12.2.0 is `neo` (`data-look="neo"` on nodes, drop-shadow filter, rounded edge corners drawn with `Q`, edges carry `data-points`), node labels are at least 120 px wide (`wrappingWidth` 120; the label `foreignObject` is 120 wide even for "A"), and a flowchart's viewBox starts at -36. 11.16.1 produced different viewBoxes for the same input (165.6 wide against 248 on GitHub for `A-->B-->C`); 12.2.0 matched GitHub exactly. Every reference here is 12.2.0.

## Items of plan 1.7
1. **Theme and font.** `theme: "dark"` when the frame's `data-color-mode` is `dark`, otherwise `default`. SVG style: `#diagram{font-family:"trebuchet ms",verdana,arial,sans-serif;font-size:16px;fill:#ccc;}`. Configuration the frame passes: `secure:["secure","securityLevel","startOnLoad","maxTextSize"]`, `securityLevel:"antiscript"`, `flowchart:{diagramPadding:48}`, `gantt:{useWidth:1200}`, `pie:{useWidth:1200}`, `sequence:{diagramMarginY:40}`. Front matter and `%%{init}%%` can still set `theme`, `look`, `layout` and the rest (they are not in `secure`); one ELK page used `theme: redux`, `look: neo` and rendered with it.
2. **Centring and background.** Frame `body` background is `rgb(13,17,23)` in dark mode (the page colour); `.render-shell` and `.mermaid-view` are transparent. `.mermaid` is `display:flex; justify-content:center; height:fit-content`; `.mermaid>svg` has `margin:0 auto`. The SVG is `width="100%"` with `style="max-width:<natural>px"`, `preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin"`, `height` set from the viewBox. So it is centred, natural size, shrinking only when the column is narrower. Frame height is `max(rendered height, 180)`, scaled by `column / viewBoxWidth` when the diagram is wider than the column. The SVG itself is transparent.
3. **ELK.** Registered. The frame registers `elk`, `elk.stress`, `elk.force`, `elk.mrtree`, `elk.sporeOverlap`, `elk.box`, `elk.rectpacking`, `dagre`, `swimlane`, `cose-bilkent`; the elk chunk (1.5 MB) is fetched when a diagram asks for it. On 11 diagrams from four public pages, rendering the same source locally with elk gave the identical SVG on 9 (the other 2 used the redux theme and local fonts differed); dagre differed on all of them. A port must implement ELK layered or accept a visible difference on `layout: elk` diagrams. No iconify packs and no tidy-tree layout are registered.
4. **Controls.** Inside the frame: a 3x3 grid, always visible (no hover rule), bottom 12 px right 12 px, 32x32 buttons, gap 2.4 px, Primer `btn` style (background `rgb(33,40,48)`, border `1px solid rgb(61,68,77)`, radius 6, icon fill `rgb(240,246,252)`). Cells: zoom-in (row 1, col 3), up (1,2), left (2,1), reset (2,2), right (2,3), down (3,2), zoom-out (3,3). Octicons zoom-in, zoom-out, sync, chevron-up/down/left/right. Zoom step 0.1, clamped 0.5 to 8, pan step 100 px, applied as `transform: translate(Xpx, Ypx) scale(S)` on the SVG with a 0.1 s ease. In the page, outside the frame, always visible at the block's top right: an expand button (arrows icon, 34x34, margin 8) and a copy button ("Copy mermaid code", copy icon turning into a check, tooltip "Copied!"). Expand opens a modal dialog (fixed, 1152 wide, radius 6, background page colour, border `rgb(61,68,77)`, padding 16, close button top right) holding a second frame at the dialog's width and the same height as the inline one.
5. **Error box.** The frame throws the message to the page. The page hides the iframe (`display:none`) and shows `.js-render-enrichment-fallback`: a `div.flash.flash-error` (1 px solid `rgba(248,81,73,0.4)`, radius 6, padding 20 px 16 px, transparent background, text `rgb(240,246,252)`, proportional page font, not monospace) containing `<p><b>Unable to render rich display</b></p>` (weight 600, 16 px margin below) and a `<p>` with the message lines separated by `<br>`. White space collapses, so the caret line does not line up. Message = Mermaid's error message, then `For more information, see https://docs.github.com/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/creating-diagrams#creating-mermaid-diagrams` (the frame builds the text from a template string, so there are 4 and 8 spaces of indentation that collapse). Directly under the box, with no gap, comes the **source code as a normal code block** (`pre lang="mermaid"`, background `rgb(21,27,35)`, padding 16, radius 6, monospace 13.6 px). The section has 16 px bottom margin. Seen message: a stateDiagram with hyphenated state ids gave `Parse error on line 2: ... Expecting 'SPACE', 'NL', ... got 'INVALID'`.
6. **Font Awesome and links.** `fa:fa-x` becomes `<i class="fa fa-twitter"></i>`; no Font Awesome CSS or font is loaded in the frame (`document.fonts` empty), the `<i>` is 0 px wide and draws nothing. `click A "url"` and `click A href "url"` produce `<a xlink:href=... target="_parent">` (the frame forces `target="_parent"` on every link, overriding `_blank`), underlined, accent colour via `.mermaid a{color:var(--fgColor-accent)!important}`. `click A callback` and `call fn()` produce no anchor (the tooltip text goes to the node's `title`).
7. **Capital M.** "```Mermaid" does not render as a diagram. The page shows a syntax-highlighted code block (`highlight highlight-source-mermaid`).

## Other findings
- GitHub decodes HTML entities in the block source before rendering and passes the source with its trailing newline, so error line numbers count that extra line.
- Sanitising: DOMPurify with an explicit allow list of SVG tags plus `b blockquote br dd div dl dt em foreignObject h1-h8 hr i li ul ol p pre span strike strong table tbody td tfoot th thead tr`.
- **Font-family quirk (trailing `;`): not present on GitHub's 12.2.0 frame.** Page https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/mermaid@11.16.1/docs/syntax/sequenceDiagram.md, frame DOM. Computed `font-family` of the root SVG and of every checked `text` (actor boxes and message text) is `"trebuchet ms", verdana, arial, sans-serif`, 16 px. Measured `getBBox().width` against canvas `measureText` in the same frame, with Trebuchet MS installed: "Hello John, how are you?" 179.88 px (Trebuchet 179.75, sans-serif 180.55, serif 163.96); "Great!" 46.39 (Trebuchet 46.39, serif 40.86); "John" 33.95 (Trebuchet 33.70, serif 30.23); "Alice" 36.64 (Trebuchet 35.37). So text is laid out in Trebuchet, not the default serif. Not checked: the sequence actor `fontFamily` default of "Open Sans" (actor text in this frame also computes to the Trebuchet list), and machines without Trebuchet.
